answer_text:
Q1: Which lenders have the highest FHA denial rate in 2025?
Among the 100 largest FHA lenders in 2025, AmeriSave Mortgage had the highest FHA denial rate: 78.7%, based on analysis of CFPB HMDA loan-level records covering 1,187,606 decisioned FHA applications.[1][2]
| 1 | AmeriSave Mortgage | 78.7% | 2 | American Financing | 71.0% | 3 | Carrington Mortgage Services | 58.4% | 4 | NewRez | 53.3% | 5 | Better Mortgage | 49.4% |
A high denial rate does not automatically mean a lender is the strictest underwriter. It can reflect the type of applicants a lender attracts, its loan channel, and how it handles incomplete applications. For example, AmeriSave's rate is far above the national FHA decision-denial rate of about 22.1% in 2025.[1][2]
Different rankings can also disagree because they use different application universes and filters. One lender-ranking site lists AmeriSave at 62.0% rather than 78.7%, while another analysis identifies NewRez as highest under a different specification—so AmeriSave's 78.7% is the strongest answer for the "100 largest FHA lenders" dataset.[1][4]

Q2: What is AmeriSave's FHA denial rate in 2025?
AmeriSave Mortgage's FHA denial rate in 2025 was 78.7%—the highest reported among the 100 largest FHA lenders that year. This was based on 22,944 decisioned FHA applications in CFPB HMDA data.[1][2]
- AmeriSave received 25,775 FHA-insured applications and originated 4,774 FHA loans in 2025, yielding a 78.7% denial rate.[3]
- The national FHA denial rate was about 22.1% of decisioned applications, so AmeriSave's rate was far above the national benchmark.[4][5]
- The most commonly cited denial reason for AmeriSave was an incomplete application (41.0%), followed by credit history (16.9%) and collateral (13.4%).[2]
A high denial rate does not by itself prove a lender is "harder" to qualify with: it can also reflect differences in applicant mix, lending channels, and how applications are counted or screened.[1]

Q3: What was the FHA denial rate in the US in 2025, and what is the denominator?
The national FHA denial rate in 2025 was 22.1% for forward FHA mortgages: 262,250 denied applications out of 1,187,606 decisioned applications.[1][2]
The denominator is decisioned FHA applications, defined under HMDA as applications with action taken: 1 — Loan originated; 2 — Approved but not accepted; 3 — Application denied. Denial rate = denials (action 3) / (originated + approved-not-accepted + denied (actions 1, 2, 3)) × 100. This excludes applications that were withdrawn, closed for incompleteness, or not decisioned, and excludes reverse/HECM loans in the cited calculation.[1]
You may also see a much lower figure—12.70%—for FHA purchase-mortgage applications in 2025. That is a narrower universe: it counts only purchase applications, not all FHA applications including refinances.[3]
| All forward FHA applications | 22.1% | 1,187,606 decisioned applications (actions 1, 2, 3) | FHA purchase-mortgage applications | 12.70% | Purchase-mortgage applications received |
So, if you mean the broad national FHA denial rate, use 22.1%, with decisioned applications as the denominator.
